title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RB_0LE1LD_1LB1LA_0RA1LF_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RB_0LE1LD_1LB1LA_0RA1LF_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run is a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by three cells per tick, and tick k applies one map P to the word beside the block exactly 2k times. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The clock is proved in Lean for every k and every word: if P takes the word through 2k trips, the tick happens, in an exactly known number of steps. What P does to the word, and what happens when a trip does not come back (the end of a phase), is not proved. An exact accelerated simulator, checked against the direct one at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, follows the run to 1.46·1013 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 218 cells have been visited and 55 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: The self-loops of the table cross runs of any length: sweep_B1, for every length and every tape around.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F on 1. F is entered only from E on 1 (1LF), and E only from C on 0 (0LE): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 with two 1s to its left, 1 1 C>0. Both directions are proved in Lean, by a case split on the cells the head reads: a configuration halts two steps later if and only if it is 1 1 C>0 (halt_iff_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: The phases in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: At every visit of the left end in state B on a 0, the tape starts with a block of 1s. Along a phase that block grows by 3 per visit; 3 phases of 4 or more visits occur in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps, the last from step 51,738,209 (1^4) to step 13,776,774,060 (1^55). The gap between visits doubles: its last ratio is 2.0000.

claims.title: The sweep and the merge
claims.text: rule_sweep: 0 0 0 D> 0 1^(3+3n) 0 becomes 0 1 0^(5+3n) B> 0 (the block is swept into 0s) in 3n+10 steps; rule_merge: 0 1 0 D>0 becomes D>0 1 1 1 in 3 steps, for every n and all tapes around.

claims.title: The clock, for every k
claims.text: tick: for every k, every word W and all tapes L, if W reaches W' by 2k P-steps (each one a trip L 0^4 B> 0 W → L D> 0 1^3 0 W') of total cost E, then L 0 0 0 D> 0 1^(3+3k) 0 W reaches L D> 0 1^(3+3k+3) 0 W' in exactly E + 16·2k − 3 steps. By strong induction on k: the sweep, one P-step, the ticks 0, …, k−1 (each eats three of the 0s), the merge.

claims.title: The exact accelerated run
claims.text: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py simulates cell by cell, but does a tick at once when its 2k P-steps all come back (the theorem above; P computed by running the machine with the small ticks inside it done at once, P2k memoized on the part of the word it reads). It gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at all 45 visits of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, and follows the run to step 1.46·1013 without a halt; the phases with 3 or more ticks start at steps 461, 1,396, 3,246,458, 51,738,209 and 213,231,975,889, the longest reaching 1^61.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.2·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1.2·1011 steps without a halt. Its visits of the left end at steps 26,873,638,645 and 53,065,176,208 keep the block 1^55 while the next block of the word grows by 3 (1^55 0 1^11 → 1^14 → 1^17): a clock on the second block, not covered by the theorem (its left context is 1^55 0, not three 0s).

claims.title: The clock test (before the proof)
claims.text: In the phase from step 51,738,209 the word at the visit with block 1^(4+3k+3) is the word at the one before after exactly 2<sup>k</sup> applications of P (the tick from block 1^4, run by the machine), for k = 0, …, 9.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: A normal tick cannot halt (the clock theorem). Halting needs a P-step that does not come back — at the end of a phase, or in the second-level clock — followed by C on a 0 with two 1s to its left (1 1 C>0). Open: what P does over 2k trips, what a phase end builds, and the second-level clock.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by three cells per tick, and tick k applies one map P to the word beside the block 2<sup>k</sup> times. The clock is proved in Lean for every tick whose 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return; an exact accelerated run follows it to 1.46·10<sup>13</sup> steps.

facts.text: Whenever its 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return, tick k applies P exactly 2<sup>k</sup> times, for every k and every word (Lean).
Steps followed by the exact accelerated run, no halt.
Needs C on 0 with 1 1 to its left (1 1 C>0); not seen.

sections.heading: A counter that doubles its time at every tick
html: Watch the tape at each moment the head, in state B, stands at the left end on a 0. The tape starts with a block of 1s, and along a phase it grows by three cells per visit while each visit takes twice as long as the previous one. The start of the last phase seen in a run of 2·1010 steps (step, tape, steps since the previous visit):
To the right of the block lies a word of short blocks (mostly 1 and 1^3, separated by single 0s). The gaps double: 218,847, 437,649, 875,333, 1,750,669, 3,501,341 steps. The next section says why.

sections.heading: The block counts, the word sees one map
html: One step before each visit the head is in state D on the 0 just left of the block: write J(k, W) for D>0 1^(3+3k) 0 W, the visit then showing the block 1^(4+3k). With three 0s on its left, J(k, W) becomes J(k+1, W') three cells further left, and W' is W with one map P applied exactly 2k times.

How a tick works: the block is swept into 0s (0 0 0 D>0 1^(3+3k) 0 → 0 1 0^(5+3k) B>0); the head makes one trip through the word (a P-step, which ends with D>0 1^3 0 on the four rightmost 0s); then the ticks 0, 1, …, k−1 run one after the other on the 0s left behind, each eating three of them; finally 0 1 0 D>0 becomes D>0 1 1 1. The number of trips is 1 + 1 + 2 + … + 2k−1 = 2k, and the tick takes exactly E + 16·2k − 3 steps when the trips take E.

This is proved in Lean for every k and every word (lean/Clock.lean, by strong induction on k), with the sweep and the merge proved by symbolic execution. It is the clock of the five machines of 1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE, with growth 3 and the head on the 0 left of the block; the same generator writes both proofs. Here a trip is long: it turns every block of the word into 0s on its way right and rebuilds the word on its way back, with small ticks of the same kind inside.

sections.heading: A phase ends when a trip does not come back
html: Whatever P does, the theorem says the clock keeps ticking as long as every trip comes back. When one does not, the phase ends and the tape is reorganized. The phases with 3 or more ticks of the exact accelerated run (checked against the direct simulator at every visit of the left end up to step 2·1010):

After the phase that reached 1^55 something new happens: the next visits, at steps 26,873,638,645 and 53,065,176,208, still show 1^55, but the block after it grows by three each time (1^55 0 1^11, 1^14, 1^17) with the time doubling: a second clock, one block further right, whose ticks have 1^55 0 on their left instead of three 0s. The theorem does not cover it, so after step 1.41·1013, where the same happens, the accelerated run only advances by small ticks and was stopped at 1.46·1013.

sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is F on 1. F is entered only from E on 1 (1LF), and E only from C on 0 (0LE): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 0 with two 1s to its left, 1 1 C>0. A tick whose trips all come back cannot halt (it is proved to reach its end), so a halt could only come at a trip that does not come back. Deciding the question needs what P does to the word over many trips, what a phase end builds, and the second clock — none of which is known in closed form.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.12). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).
After 109 steps the tape spans 218 cells (121 left of the start, 89 right), with a density of 1s of 0.252.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A clock: at each visit of the left end in state B the block 1^(4+3k) has grown by 3, and the word to its right has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one trip of the head through the word) — proved in Lean for every k, for each tick whose 2^k trips all return; a phase ends when P fails to come back. Exact accelerated run to 1.46·10<sup>13</sup> steps, no halt. Halting needs C on a 0 with two 1s to its left (1 1 C>0).
